title: Head movement compensation in real-time magnetoencephalographic recordings
author: Little, Boe, et al.

steps.title: Preprocess 1‑s MEG segment
steps.instruction: For each one‑second data segment sent to the real‑time computer, apply the cross‑talk correction matrix, baseline‑correct each sensor using the segment mean, decompose the signal at each HPI coil frequency to obtain sine (real) and cosine (imaginary) components, plot these components for all sensors on a complex plane, perform linear regression, and project each sensor’s components onto the regression line to obtain the magnetic field strength (the “measured” MEG field) for each coil.

substeps.instruction: Apply cross‑talk correction matrix to eliminate inter‑sensor interference.
Baseline‑correct each sensor using the mean amplitude over the 1‑s segment.
Perform continuous signal decomposition at each HPI coil frequency to obtain sine and cosine components.
Plot the two components for all sensors on a complex plane.
Fit a linear regression to the plotted data.
Project each sensor’s components onto the regression line to derive magnetic field strength at the coil frequency (measured field).

steps.title: Rigorous coil localization (localizer)
steps.instruction: Using the final one‑second segment of the localizer scan, estimate each HPI coil’s position, orientation, and magnitude with an unconstrained Nelder‑Mead simplex optimization applied three times per coil (first magnitude only, then orientation only, finally location only), starting from the acquisition software’s initial head‑position estimate; the resulting six parameters per coil define a rigid body of the four coils.

substeps.instruction: Provide initial parameters from the acquisition software’s head‑position estimate.
Run Nelder‑Mead optimization allowing only dipole magnitude to vary (first pass).
Run Nelder‑Mead optimization allowing only dipole orientation to vary (second pass).
Run Nelder‑Mead optimization allowing only dipole location to vary (third pass).
Combine the optimized parameters of all four coils to define a rigid body.

steps.title: Real‑time head position estimation
steps.instruction: For every subsequent one‑second data segment, compute the measured fields for the four coils, then run a single six‑parameter constrained active‑set optimization that translates and rotates the rigid body to minimize the least‑squares error between measured and calculated fields, constraining translation to ≤1 cm and rotation to ≤3° per axis, using the previous segment’s transform as the initial guess; retain only the three coils with the lowest error for the fit and save the resulting coordinate‑frame transformation matrix.

substeps.instruction: Calculate measured magnetic fields for all four HPI coils.
Set up a six‑parameter active‑set optimization (translation + rotation).
Constrain the optimization to ≤1 cm translation and ≤3° rotation on each axis.
Initialize the algorithm with the transform from the previous segment.
Select the three coils that yield the lowest least‑squares error for error calculation.
Save the resulting transformation matrix to file.

steps.title: Post‑experiment coil trajectory calculation
steps.instruction: After each experiment, apply the saved transformation matrices to reconstruct HPI coil positions over time, and run the vendor‑supplied MaxFilter offline HPI analysis for the same data to enable direct comparison between real‑time and offline coil‑position estimates.

substeps.instruction: Load each segment’s transformation matrix and compute the corresponding coil positions.
Run MaxFilter’s offline HPI routine to obtain coil positions for each second.
Compare real‑time and offline coil‑position time courses.

steps.title: Real‑time trial extraction and averaging
steps.instruction: When a data segment contains an event marker for a phantom current source, extract a trial from –100 ms to +200 ms relative to the marker, baseline‑correct to the trial mean, apply a Hanning window and a 40 Hz low‑pass filter, then baseline‑correct again using the 50 ms pre‑onset interval; continuously update the inter‑trial average and display it for quality control, and after 100 trials extract the measured field at the 31 ms post‑onset peak latency.

substeps.instruction: Isolate trials spanning –100 ms to +200 ms around each event marker.
Baseline‑correct each trial to its mean amplitude.
Apply a Hanning window and low‑pass filter at 40 Hz.
Perform a second baseline correction using the 50 ms preceding activation onset.
Update and display the running inter‑trial average.
After accumulating 100 trials, record the measured field at 31 ms latency.

steps.title: Equivalent current dipole modeling
steps.instruction: For each current source, perform a grid‑search ECD fit on a spherical grid (radius = 8 cm, spacing = 1 cm) centered on the MEG origin, calculating three dipoles (one per cardinal axis) at each grid point and selecting the position with the lowest least‑squares error; then refine this estimate with an unconstrained BFGS non‑linear least‑squares optimization starting from the grid location and a zero‑magnitude moment.

substeps.instruction: Generate a spherical grid (8 cm radius, 1 cm spacing) around the MEG system origin.
At each grid point, compute three dipoles aligned with the X, Y, and Z axes.
Calculate the least‑squares error between measured and modeled fields for each dipole.
Select the grid point/dipole combination with the minimum error as the initial ECD.
Run BFGS optimization, allowing position and orientation to vary, starting from the grid‑derived location and a moment of zero magnitude.

steps.title: Calculate rtSE peak‑to‑peak magnitude
steps.instruction: In offline analysis, detect local extrema automatically in the rtSE data for each current‑source activation, compute the peak‑to‑peak magnitude, average these magnitudes across all activations at each stationary phantom position to obtain a mean source amplitude, and calculate the percent change of this mean relative to the scan start.

substeps.instruction: Run the automated local‑extrema detection algorithm on rtSE activation data.
Calculate peak‑to‑peak magnitude for each activation.
Average magnitudes for all activations at each stationary phantom position.
Determine the percent change of each position’s mean amplitude relative to the initial scan mean.

steps.title: Offline HPI and source analysis
steps.instruction: Run MaxFilter to obtain HPI coil positions for each second of data, compute coil displacements and derive phantom velocity, apply SSS movement compensation, perform offline source estimation with the vendor software, and calculate peak‑to‑peak magnitudes of the current‑source activations using the same automated extrema method as for rtSE data.

substeps.instruction: Execute MaxFilter’s HPI routine to get coil positions per second.
Calculate inter‑second coil displacements and estimate phantom velocity.
Apply Signal Space Separation (SSS) movement compensation to the MEG data.
Run the vendor‑supplied offline source‑estimation pipeline.
Detect local extrema and compute peak‑to‑peak magnitudes for the offline source data.
